institutions.title: Poder imperial y sucesión severiana
institutions.text: La presencia de varios augustos o césares no significa varios Estados nacionales. Los títulos y mandatos del año se muestran por separado.
institutions.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

institutions.title: Crisis imperial y autoridades rivales
institutions.text: Emperadores de breve mandato, asociaciones imperiales y pretendientes regionales; no todos gobernaron al mismo tiempo ni todo el territorio de la compilación.

institutions.title: Año de los seis emperadores
institutions.text: Gordianos, Pupieno, Balbino y Maximino se suceden o enfrentan. Gordiano III aparece con su dignidad de césar y después como augusto, no como dos personas.
institutions.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

institutions.title: Captura de Valeriano en la campaña oriental
institutions.text: Episodio de la guerra con Shapur I; el punto regional no reconstruye el perímetro exacto del control sasánida.
institutions.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

institutions.title: Reintegración del poder galo
institutions.text: La derrota de Tétrico en274 termina el poder imperial galo rival. Su contorno heredado posterior se consulta bajo el marco romano, sin prolongar esa entidad hasta282.
institutions.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

institutions.title: Primera tetrarquía
institutions.text: Diocleciano y Maximiano son augustos; Constancio y Galerio, césares. Las cuatro sedes de referencia no equivalen a cuatro Estados soberanos.
institutions.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

''[[Zeitschrift für Papyrologie und Epigraphik|ZPE]]'' '''9''', 1–19. No contemporary or later sources give any definitive conclusion.</ref>
1 May 305 – 25 July 306 (with [[Galerius]] in the [[Eastern Roman Empire|East]])
{{ubl|20 November 284 – 1 April 286|1 April 286 – 1 May 305 ([[Eastern Roman Empire|East]])}}

1 March 293{{efn|The earlier dates for Galerius's appointment have been argued for based on the suggestion that the appointments of Constantius and Galerius were timed to coincide (Barnes 1981, 8–9; Southern 1999, 146). Barnes (1982, 62) argues against a dating of 21 May 293 in Nicomedia originating in Seston, ''Dioclétien'', 88ff., stating that the evidence adduced (the 7th-century [[Chronicon Paschale|Paschal Chronicle]] [https://archive.org/details/chronicon-p/page/2/mode/1up Ol.268] and the contemporary [[Lactantius]], ''[[De mortibus persecutorum|DMP]]'' 19.2) is invalid and confused. Lactantius is commenting on Diocletian and the place where Diocletian was acclaimed, and that the "Maximianus" in the text is therefore a later gloss; the Paschal Chronicle is not authoritative for this period for events outside Egypt, and may simply be commenting on the day when the laureled image of the new emperors arrived in Alexandria. Moreover, Lactantius ([https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/0705.htm ''DMP'' 35]) explicitly states that Galerius's ''[[dies imperii]]'' fell on 1 March. Potter (2004, 650) agrees that locating the acclamation to Nicomedia is false, but believes that Seston's other evidence makes a strong case for a temporal lag between the two Caesars' acclamations.}} – 1 May 305 (under [[Diocletian]]){{sfn|Barnes|1982|p=4}}

{{circa}} March – April 238<ref name=Rea>The exact chronology of events is unknown. See: Rea, J. (1972). "[http://www.jstor.org/stable/20180380 O. Leid. 144 and the Chronology of A.D. 238]". ''[[Zeitschrift für Papyrologie und Epigraphik|ZPE]]'' '''9''', 1-19.</ref>

{{circa}} March – April 238<ref name=Rea>The exact chronology of events is unknown. See: Rea, J. (1972). "[http://www.jstor.org/stable/20180380 O. Leid. 144 and the Chronology of A.D. 238]". ''[[Zeitschrift für Papyrologie und Epigraphik|ZPE]]'' '''9''', 1-19.</ref>
1 April 286 – 1 May 305 {{awrap|(with Diocletian in [[Eastern Roman Empire|the East]])}}

March 235 – {{circa}} June 238{{efn|name=death|His death is sometimes dated to 24 June. This is based on the "3 years 4 months 2 days" reign-length given by the ''[[Chronograph of 354]]''. Some interpret this as "3 years 3 months 2 days", which gives 24 June reckoning from 22 March 235, the supposed date of Alexander's death (the exact date is disputed).<ref name=rea/> Maximinus's official {{lang|la|[[dies imperii]]}} (day of accession) was almost certainly 23 March, but the figures of the ''Chronograph'' can not be trusted as they are often corrupted, inaccurate or made-up.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Burgess |first=Richard W. |url=https://www.steiner-verlag.de/en/Roman-Imperial-Chronology-and-Early-Fourth-Century-Historiography/9783515107327 |title=Roman imperial chronology and early-fourth-century historiography |date=2014 |publisher=Steiner |isbn=978-3-515-10732-7 |series=Historia Einzelschriften |location=Stuttgart|pages=67–69, 93–95}}</ref> [[Papyri]] show that the Gordians were recognized in Egypt between 7 April and 13 June. Maximinus is not mentioned again, as he was declared an enemy by the Senate. Peachin argues that he died in early June,<ref>{{cite book|last=Peachin|first=Michael|url=https://archive.org/details/ritac235/page/n24/mode/1up?view=theater|title=Roman Imperial Titulature and Chronology, A.D. 235–284|publisher=Gieben|year=1990|isbn=90-5063-034-0|place=Amsterdam}}</ref> but all we know is that he died during the reign of Pupienus and Balbinus, between May and August according to papyri.<ref name=rea>{{Cite journal|last=Rea|first=J. R.|date=1972|title=O. Leid. 144 and the Chronology of A. D. 238|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/20180380|journal=Zeitschrift für Papyrologie und Epigraphik|volume=9|pages=1–19|jstor=20180380}}</ref>}}

''[[Zeitschrift für Papyrologie und Epigraphik|ZPE]]'' '''9''', 1–19. No contemporary or later sources give any definitive conclusion.</ref>

9 April 193 – {{awrap|4 February 211}}<ref>{{Cite book|last=Kienast|first=Dietmar|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=rYRorgEACAAJ|title=Römische Kaisertabelle Grundzüge einer römischen Kaiserchronologie|publisher=Wissenschaftliche Buchgesellschaft|year=2017|isbn=978-3-534-07532-4|edition=6|location=Darmstadt|pages=149–159|chapter=Septimius Severus (9 Apr. 193–4 Febr. 211)|oclc=75671165|orig-year=1990}}</ref>

contexts.title: Poder imperial y sucesión severiana
contexts.text: La presencia de varios augustos o césares no significa varios Estados nacionales. Los títulos y mandatos del año se muestran por separado.
contexts.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

contexts.title: Crisis imperial y autoridades rivales
contexts.text: Emperadores de breve mandato, asociaciones imperiales y pretendientes regionales; no todos gobernaron al mismo tiempo ni todo el territorio de la compilación.
contexts.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

contexts.title: Año de los seis emperadores
contexts.text: Gordianos, Pupieno, Balbino y Maximino se suceden o enfrentan. Gordiano III aparece con su dignidad de césar y después como augusto, no como dos personas.
contexts.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

contexts.title: Captura de Valeriano en la campaña oriental
contexts.text: Episodio de la guerra con Shapur I; el punto regional no reconstruye el perímetro exacto del control sasánida.
contexts.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

contexts.title: Reintegración del poder galo
contexts.text: La derrota de Tétrico en274 termina el poder imperial galo rival. Su contorno heredado posterior se consulta bajo el marco romano, sin prolongar esa entidad hasta282.
contexts.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.

contexts.title: Primera tetrarquía
contexts.text: Diocleciano y Maximiano son augustos; Constancio y Galerio, césares. Las cuatro sedes de referencia no equivalen a cuatro Estados soberanos.
contexts.note: Contexto parcial; no inventario completo de hechos o conflictos.
